title: Primary Key
body:
The column (or combination of columns) that uniquely identifies each row in a table — the unique inventory tag on every item. The database enforces that it is unique and never null, and it's the handle everything else uses to refer to that row.

Most tables use a surrogate key: an auto-incrementing integer `id`, or a UUID, with no business meaning. The alternative is a natural key drawn from the data itself (an ISBN, an email address), which reads better but breaks badly when the real-world value turns out to change. A primary key is automatically indexed (see [[Database Index]]), and it's what a [[Foreign Key]] on another table points at. See [[SQL]].
